scenario: Fresh active workspace from one fenced source, preserved provenance and new authority

stages.label: fenced-source-and-old-copy
stages.explanation: The current source is stopped; its earlier snapshot remains quarantined. A new destination has not been created.

stages.label: old-secret-rejected-before-transfer
stages.explanation: A credential already issued in the source cannot become the new administrator's credential.

stages.label: fresh-active-baseline-and-fenced-history
stages.explanation: The new workspace imports accepted content and exact dependency records at revision R, starts with only a fresh administrator, and preserves old history separately.

stages.label: completed-replay-and-single-target-binding
stages.explanation: The exact request returns its original fact without new events; another destination or operation conflicts.

stages.label: old-authority-and-active-copy-rejected
stages.explanation: Old credentials and proposals do not acquire new authority; source and archive stay fenced, and a bare active database copied to another path is rejected.

stages.label: fresh-authenticated-authors-and-composition
stages.explanation: New role grants authorize three new author jobs and one composition. No old lease or opinion is reused.

stages.label: fresh-opinions-and-new-acceptance
stages.explanation: Four new scoped opinions and a new coordinator authorize a new acceptance in the destination, advancing R to R+1.

stages.label: updated-release-retains-provenance
stages.explanation: The updated destination release loads with complete dependency records; unchanged imported artifacts still use their original baseline.

stages.label: new-workspace-backup-and-historical-restore
stages.explanation: An ordinary backup and restore preserve imported provenance and the new receipt; quarantine takes priority over the live destination's path binding.

stages.label: old-source-remains-stopped-and-history-preserved
stages.explanation: New work and its backup leave the old source, full history archive and older snapshot unchanged; the completed transfer remains one historical fact.

limits: The source-side single-target reservation and destination path binding are cooperative local controls, not an external fencing service.
The active destination contains accepted content and preserved dependency descriptors; old runtime grants, leases, tasks, opinions and receipts remain in the separate fenced archive.
All new decisions are programmed local opinions under fresh grants; they do not establish independent people, factual truth or semantic equivalence.
Release loader compatibility and exact baseline dependencies preserve the existing declared freshness checks; a separately induced stale imported read/query case is not performed here.
Bare destination copying is demonstrated through SQLite backup into a new private file; it is not a corrupted SQL fixture or simulated process crash.
Public observations omit only governance_status's changing top-level observed_at for equality; raw timestamps and addressed proof bodies remain intact.
The new destination's ordinary backup stays a quarantined historical snapshot. It does not reactivate a live copied database or any old source authority.
The destination's ordinary database backup does not embed its separate full ancestral history.sqlite3 archive; that archive remains a separate private transfer artifact.
Old software and a trusted database owner using raw SQL can bypass the cooperative path. Existing external publication effects are not revoked or replayed by the transfer.
